title: adaptive-precision-cascade-design-notes
content:
Context and objective:
We need a lightweight, generalizable inference pattern for mid-market customers running extraction and summarization workloads with strong cost constraints and bursty traffic. The goal is a POC design that combines small/quantized models for the bulk of traffic with automatic escalation to larger (higher-precision) variants when confidence or downstream quality metrics indicate a likely failure.

Key constraints / customer asks:
- 99th percentile latency target: 350ms for short queries (<= 256 tokens) during steady state.
- Cost target: reduce token spend by ~3x vs baseline fp16 single-model endpoint.
- Sensitive data: on-prem private deployment option; no external retrieval allowed during canary.
- Can support asynchronous fallback (best-effort) but primary path should be online (sync) for UI flows.

High-level approach (Adaptive-Precision Cascade):
1) Route incoming request to a fast, highly-quantized model (candidate: quantized 4-bit or Q4_0 variant) with aggressive batching and prefix KV caching.
2) Evaluate a lightweight quality/confidence check on model output (heuristic scorer + learned regressor).
3) If quality score < threshold, escalate to a mid-tier model (8-bit quantized fp8-like or int8 dynamic) with higher capacity and slightly higher latency.
4) Final fallback to fp16/float32 variant for critical failures or when downstream eval metrics are poor.
5) Telemetry-driven thresholding: adjust thresholds based on per-customer precision targets and observed QA regressions.

Model candidates considered and rationale:
- tiny-qa-q4 (Q4_0 7B variant): excellent token throughput, low memory, best for warm-cache prefix-heavy workloads. Risk: hallucination on long-context prompts.
- mid-qa-q8 (8-bit 13B variant): good middle ground for accuracy vs latency. Use for second-tier escalation.
- large-qa-fp16 (13-30B FP16): fallback for high-importance queries and for offline retraining dataset collection.
- instruction-tuned retrieval-augmented variants: used when RAG is enabled; must be isolated for PII-sensitive customers.

Quantization strategy (adaptive & workload-aware):
- Use per-model quant profiles rather than one-size-fits-all. For each candidate model we ship a profile: static Q4 for tiny, dynamic Q8 for mid-tier, fp16 for fallback.
- Hybrid precision on KV cache: store KV in 8-bit quant for retrieval, but compute attention with mixed precision where possible to keep latency consistent.
- Inference pipeline will allow runtime switch: if sequence length > 512 or tokens look 'complex' (e.g., many code blocks), force mid-tier directly.
- For private/on-prem installs we provide a config knob: prefer deterministic fp16 if hardware repro is required.

Prompt/pipeline tuning notes (practical heuristics):
- System prompt minimalism: keep system role to 1-2 short sentences. Longer system instructions reduce effective context for models more sensitive to quantization.
- Chunking: for long inputs, chunk + local summarization before main LM call to reduce tokens and improve prefix cache hit rates.
- Few-shot examples: place exemplars after system message but before user content to maximize prefix cache reuse across similar requests.
- Safety templates: add short post-processing checklist (regex/exact-match filters) to catch deterministic PII patterns before escalation.

Confidence & scoring (fast, cheap checks):
- Heuristic 1: generation entropy proxy — compute token-level average log-prob using model logprobs when available; if < X -> escalate.
- Heuristic 2: repetition/degeneration detector (n-gram repeat > threshold leads to escalate).
- Learned regressor: small logistic regressor trained on recent labeled examples (features: length, avg logprob, ROUGE vs retrieved context if RAG used, metadata flags). Regessor runs in < 5ms.
- Conservative default thresholds for POC; tune with A/B experiments.

Routing & runtime policies:
- Smart-routing priorities: prefer warm-cache instances in same region/tier; otherwise use cost-tier routing.
- Burst handling: if dedicated pool saturated, fall back to cheaper quantized pool with longer tail but accept occasional async fallback.
- Canary rollout plan: 5% traffic to cascade enabled path vs 95% baseline; monitor token-accuracy delta and p95 latency.

Telemetry & metrics to collect (per-request):
- model_variant, quant_profile, route_taken, upstream_latency_ms, model_processing_ms, token_count_in/out, avg_token_logprob, confidence_score, escalation_flag, cost_estimate_per_request.
- SLOs to track: p50/p95 latency, accuracy proxy (synthetic eval set), escalation rate (target < 8% for steady state), cost per 1k requests.

Experiment matrix (quick plan for POC week 1):
- Variables: model_variant (tiny-q4, mid-q8, large-fp16), batch_size (1, 4, 8), kv_cache (warm vs cold), prompt-template (short vs long), reranker on/off.
- Metrics: latency p50/p95, tokens per response, escalation rate, synthetic QA accuracy (F1/EM) on gold set.
- Run small grid overnight using dedicated 4-GPU node + one 8-GPU fallback.

Quick benchmark (synthetic numbers from initial lab run) — results illustrative, not final:
- tiny-q4 batch=1 warm-cache: p50=42ms, p95=180ms, escalation_rate=12%, synthetic_F1=0.68, cost~$0.12 perk tokens
- mid-q8 batch=1 warm-cache: p50=95ms, p95=250ms, escalation_rate=4%, synthetic_F1=0.82, cost~$0.35 perk tokens
- large-fp16 batch=1 warm-cache: p50=210ms, p95=520ms, escalation_rate=0.9%, synthetic_F1=0.91, cost~$1.20 perk tokens
Interpretation: tiny-q4 is clearly cheapest but needs a higher mid-tier routing rate or tuned prompts. Target is to push escalation < 8% while staying within p95 budget.

Runbook highlights (for SEs running the POC):
- 0) Pre-check: ensure KV cache warmed by seeding with top 100 recent queries for customer domain.
- 1) Deploy tiny-q4 endpoint with logging enabled (token-level logprobs). Start 1000 synthetic requests, capture metrics.
- 2) Enable regressor and set conservative threshold. Monitor escalation rate and p95 latency for 30m.
- 3) If escalation rate > 15%, adjust prompt simplification and enable light reranker before escalation.
- 4) After 24h, run offline comparison of escalated examples to label for regressor retraining.

Open questions & risks:
- How to quantify "quality" for customers with subjective QA needs? Suggest collecting 500 labeled examples from users early in POC for threshold tuning.
- Quantization drift: we need to test cold-start behavior for Q4 variants — are outputs deterministic enough for compliance auditing?
- Monitoring cost attribution in mixed-route flows (assigning cost to request when it touches multiple variants).

Next steps and deliverables for POC:
- Week 0 (today): finalize model variants and quant profiles; prepare canary config and synthetic eval set. Owner: Aisha.
- Week 1: run experiment matrix, collect telemetry, iterate regressor and prompt templates. Owner: Liam.
- Week 2: prepare customer-facing report with cost/latency/accuracy tradeoffs, propose Dedicated sizing if requested. Owner: Priya.

Notes to self / quick reminders:
- Keep system prompt short for tiny-q4 to maximize effective token budget.
- Use ngram filtering as cheap safety net before escalation.
- Consider adding a tiny rule-based post-processor for highly-structured tasks (e.g., invoice fields) to avoid unnecessary escalations.

References:
- See linked Confluence spec for quant profiles and exact conversion scripts.
- JIRA- SE-2741 contains the regen data set and initial regressor training artifacts.

End of note.
